RFC 4301 Section 6.2: "If no SA exists that would carry the outbound ICMP message in question, and if no SPD entry would allow carriage of this outbound ICMP error message, then an IPsec implementation MUST map the message to the SA that would carry the return traffic associated with the packet that triggered the ICMP error message." Tested: "if no SPD entry would allow carriage of this outbound ICMP error message". Gap: "MUST map the message to the SA that would carry the return traffic associated with the packet that triggered the ICMP error message". Producer: internal/component/ike/engine/icmp_overlap.go::refuseICMPErrorBypass. Because the kernel maps an error into the return SA even where a BYPASS would carry it in clear, refuseICMPErrorBypass refuses, beside a peer with icmp-error-check true and no vti bind, unmatched bypass and every ICMP-error-carrying bypass one of whose OUT allows reaches the peer's remote selectors: an out or both entry's out half (remote prefix) and, through icmpErrorSides, an in or both entry's OUT transit gate (local prefix). The negatives prove each refusal with the exact operator error and fix: the catch-all, the out-half overlap, and TestICMPOverlapBypassTransitGate's four in or both cases (record red with icmpErrorSides reverted). The positives accept a disjoint remote prefix, echo request, an in entry with a disjoint local prefix, TCP, another family, check false and a vti bind peer, and the gate test accepts its six controls, so the refusal is tied to the condition. The corrected annotation states this. The mapping itself is not observed by any tagged test, as the gap says. Scoped evidence only; zero whole-requirement credit.
